fatal_errors: The proposed initially single-phase, grain-boundary-controlled material state conflicts with the target as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic microstructure containing FCC and B2 phases.

The hypothesis repeats the conventional segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation mechanism rather than identifying L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries as the governing mediators.

It predicts broadly increasing intergranular embrittlement after thermal exposure rather than the observed non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, with minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The proposed temperature range and boundaries omit the mechanistically important 550-750°C brittle window and the distinct behavior below 550°C and above 750°C.
explanation: The response correctly treats thermal aging as a testable intervention and proposes useful TEM/APT, toughness, and fractography measurements with an explicit falsification rule. However, its central scientific account is incompatible with the target: it invokes grain-boundary segregation and ordered precipitates, reduced boundary cohesion, and intergranular fracture—the conventional-alloy expectation the comparison was meant to distinguish. The target instead concerns a dual-phase eutectic HEA in which aging near 600°C enhances L12 ordering in FCC domains and produces jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries; elevated APBE and modulus promote planar slip and dislocation pile-ups, while boundary-tip stress concentrations trigger instability. The response also misses ductility recovery near 750°C through reduced ordering and ductile phase-boundary transition zones. Its experiment could test its own alternative, but it lacks the phase-boundary-resolved dislocation and crack-initiation observations needed to discriminate the target mechanism.
